findings.problem: The hint says acabar also means to run out, but that sense belongs to the pronominal acabarse (se acabó la leche), so a learner would memorize a wrong use of plain acabar.
findings.fix: hint: not terminar; also to end up

back.es: to finish, to end (also: to end up, with por or a gerund)
back.example: Did you already finish the homework?

note: In Rioplatense and some other varieties, plain acabar without an object is also slang for to climax, so the editor may want examples that always give it an object, as this one does.
